rules.when: Errand-grade verification and routine chores: reachability or environment checks a human would do by hand, walking a flow in a browser to confirm an entry point, starting or restarting a demo or local stack, preparing demo data, re-running an already-written verification script, and other bounded mechanical work whose steps and success criteria are already known. No root-cause search, no architectural judgement, no gnarly ambiguity.
rules.why: Errand verification runs on Luna with maximum thinking; Astra is kept for difficult investigation and planning.

rules.when: Moderately difficult engineering work below the difficult-investigation tier: a bounded root-cause diagnosis with a known reproduction path, a non-trivial fix that needs judgement but no cross-cutting redesign, or a review whose scope and method are already fixed. Harder than routine implementation, easier than unclear cross-cutting investigation.
rules.why: Sol and Opus share this tier; choose between them by comparable quota and never drop to the routine tier.

rules.when: Difficult investigations and difficult planning requiring exceptionally high reasoning: unclear or gnarly root-cause investigations, complex cross-cutting architecture redesign, or difficult planning with major unresolved tradeoffs. Ordinary engineering architecture and bounded implementation are covered by separate rules.
rules.why: Choose by quota-axi spendPriority; missing or unknown quota is not treated as headroom, and the tier is never downgraded.

rules.when: Ordinary engineering architecture work: bounded module or interface design, technical structure decisions, and normal engineering design or planning that requires architectural judgment but is not a difficult investigation or complex cross-cutting redesign. Not implementation of an already-established design.
rules.why: Ordinary architecture and design go to Opus with the 1M-context alias so long tasks do not compact early.

rules.when: Authoring or substantially rewriting a document a HUMAN will read: an internal technical proposal, architecture document, requirements breakdown, design or onboarding document for product and engineering readers. Excluded: agent-facing instructions such as an INSTALL.md runbook written for another agent to execute, code-adjacent documentation such as README updates, inline comments and changelog entries, and routine doc corrections.
rules.why: Human-facing documents pin Opus 4.6 because the floating opus alias resolves to the newest Opus.

rules.when: Implementation and routine execution with a sufficiently established design: bounded coding changes, tests, routine code-adjacent documentation such as README updates, inline comments and changelog entries, repetitive data collection, and straightforward fixes that do not require architectural decisions or difficult investigation.
rules.why: Routine implementation runs on Terra low; reclassify instead of silently widening this tier when the work turns out to need architecture or difficult investigation.
